domain_restrictions: j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1 (so n - 1 >= 0 and the interval for j is nonempty for n >= 1)
the derivative statement for H_{n,j} is asserted for all t in (0,1)
implicit: T_{n,j}(t) must lie in I_{n,j} for every t in (0,1) so that F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) is defined
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every positive integer n and every integer j with 0 <= j <= n - 1, if F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}, then H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1) and for every real t in (0,1), the derivative satisfies H'_{n,j}(t) equals F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) divided by n.
quantifier_order: for all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1
for all functions F_n that are differentiable on I_{n,j}
for all real t with t in (0,1)

variables.domain: subset of integers satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
variables.name: j
variables.role: fixed parameter indexing the intervals and maps

variables.name: t
variables.role: variable point where the derivative of H_{n,j} is evaluated

variables.name: F_n
variables.role: given differentiable function used to define H_{n,j}
variables.type: real-valued function of a real variable

variables.name: H_{n,j}
variables.role: target function whose differentiability and derivative formula are asserted
variables.type: real-valued function of a real variable

variables.name: I_{n,j}
variables.role: domain on which F_n is assumed differentiable

variables.name: T_{n,j}
variables.role: input transformation used inside F_n' in the derivative formula
variables.type: real-valued function of a real variable

witness_dependencies: H'_{n,j}(t) depends on t only through the value T_{n,j}(t) used as the input to F_n'
the divisor n appears in the scaling factor 1/n and is fixed by the outer parameters (n, j)
the existence of H'_{n,j}(t) implicitly depends on differentiability of F_n at T_{n,j}(t) and on the regularity of T_{n,j} as used in the construction of H_{n,j} (not stated explicitly)

statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. Assume F_n is differentiable on I_{n,j}. Then H_{n,j} is differentiable on (0,1), and for each real t in (0,1), H'_{n,j}(t) = F_n'(T_{n,j}(t)) / n.
